passage: Class 5 teacher's note, results day. Kavitha topped the class in the term exams and glowed all morning; twice I heard her tell the row in front what her total was. Then she noticed Ayesha folding a paper into a small square, and Kavitha stopped mid-sentence. At lunch she asked Ayesha to show her how to shade maps so neatly, and admitted her own map marks were her lowest. When I congratulated her, I said there was nothing wrong with feeling glad. She answered, "I'm really happy, but I don't want to be loud about it." I will see how she handles the next round of results. 🙂

qa.q: How many times did the teacher hear Kavitha tell the row in front what her total was?
qa.a: Twice; the teacher heard her tell the row in front what her total was.

qa.q: What was Kavitha feeling when she noticed Ayesha folding the paper, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Pride mixed with sudden thoughtfulness: she stopped mid-sentence and then asked Ayesha for help, saying she was happy but did not want to be loud.

qa.q: What would you advise Kavitha to do the next time results come out?
qa.a: Enjoy being glad, share the news quietly, and keep remembering what classmates like Ayesha are good at.

qa.q: How might Ayesha have felt when Kavitha asked for help with the maps?
qa.a: Ayesha may have felt noticed for a real strength after a disappointing morning, though it could also have stung a little; the note does not say.

grounding: Illustrates a top scorer feeling proud and choosing modest sharing while valuing a friend's strength.

passage: When Masterji read out the marks under the banyan tree, Gurpreet had the highest in Class 6 of their village school near Moga: 47 out of 50. He wanted to jump on the bench and shout it. On the way to the handpump, he waved his paper at everyone. 'Forty-seven! Beat that!' Then he saw Shalini, who had scored 29, quietly folding her paper very small. Something in his chest pinched. Shalini was the one who had shown him how to fix his cycle chain last week; he'd never have managed it alone. Gurpreet folded his own paper and put it in his pocket. 'Shalini, the chain's slipping again,' he said. 'Can you look at it after school?' She brightened. 'Bring it to the tubewell.'

qa.q: Where did Masterji read out the marks?
What was Gurpreet feeling as he waved his paper?
qa.a: Proud and excited, wanting to show off his top mark.

qa.q: How did Gurpreet change the way he shared his joy?
qa.a: He put his paper away and turned to Shalini's strength, asking her to fix his cycle chain.

qa.q: How might Shalini have felt when Gurpreet waved his paper?
qa.a: Embarrassed and small about her own mark, which is why she folded her paper so small.

grounding: A village boy who topped the class wants to show off, notices a classmate's hurt, and honours her different strength.

passage: In Mexico City, Señora Ruiz handed back the history tests, and Alejandro's had a gold star: the highest mark in the class. His whole body buzzed. At lunch he couldn't stop talking about it. 'I even got the bonus question. Nobody else did, right?' Tomas, beside him, kept eating his torta and said nothing. Alejandro stopped mid-sentence. Tomas had got a C. And Tomas was the one who drew the comics everyone passed round, the ones Alejandro could never copy. 'Sorry,' Alejandro said. 'I'm going on and on.' Tomas shrugged, but his mouth twitched. 'It's fine. You studied hard.' 'Want to make a comic about the Aztec emperor for the project? You draw, I'll write the facts.' Tomas grinned. 'Deal.'

qa.q: What did Alejandro's test have on it?
What was Alejandro feeling when he got the test back?
qa.a: Proud and excited; his whole body buzzed.

qa.q: What did Alejandro do once he noticed Tomas?
qa.a: He apologised for going on and on and suggested a project where Tomas's drawing and his own facts both mattered 👍

qa.q: How might Tomas feel during Alejandro's bragging?
qa.a: Quietly low about his C, so he kept eating and said nothing.

grounding: A boy in Mexico who topped the class catches himself showing off and remembers his friend's strengths.
